title: Servants of Christ, Arise
description: Servants of Christ, Arise in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Lydia Sigourney wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 356 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Active Piety”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ser-vants of Christ, a-rise, And gird you for the toil; The dew of pro-mise from the skies Al-rea-dy cheers the soil.

lines: And gird you for the toil;
The dew of promise from the skies
And where the sons of sorrow pine,
And wrap the Saviour's changeless love
So shall you share the wealth,
And the blest gospel's saving health

licence: Public domain: Lydia Sigourney died in 1865.
credits: Words by Lydia Sigourney (1791–1865), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
